Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard,
First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  August 22, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  August 22, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS. Mayor Butts announced that Agenda Item No. DR-5
  was being pulled from the Agenda.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas, other than the public hearings.

  There was no response.

  142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated August
  17, 2023, in the amount of $6,710,046.95, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman /
  Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 23-17 INTRODUCED -
  AMENDING OR REPEALING VARIOUS MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS
  REGULATING PEDDLING, SOLICITING, AND SIDEWALK VENDORS AND
  ADDING A NEW ARTICLE 13 “SIDEWALK VENDOR PROGRAM” TO
  CHAPTER 8 OF THE MUNICIPAL CODE. The City Clerk announced that the next
  scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider introduction of an ordinance amending
  or repealing various Municipal Code sections regulating peddling, soliciting, and sidewalk
  vendors and adding a new Article 13 “Sidewalk Vendor Program” to Chapter 8 of the
  Municipal Code to comply with changes in State Law, notice had been given in the time,
  form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were
  received.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated August 22, 2023.
 August 22, 2023

  Jerry Tucker, Code Enforcement Manager gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Marvin McCoy spoke opposing the "Sidewalk Vendor Program." He stated that imposing
  the 1,000-foot radius was addressed in the State Senate Bill, and approving this Agenda
  Item would only expand the State Senate Bill. He mentioned it being a de facto ban on
  vending. McCoy discussed the City Attorney's comments concerning vendor lawsuits. He
  also discussed the unnecessary legal actions this could bring.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:06 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 23-17 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING OR REPEALING VARIOUS MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS
  REGULATING PEDDLING, SOLICITING, AND SIDEWALK VENDING AND
  ADDING A NEW ARTICLE 13 “SIDEWALK VENDOR PROGRAM” TO
  CHAPTER 8 OF THE MUNICIPAL CODE TO COMPLY WITH CHANGES IN
  STATE LAW

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

301  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 23-00004
  (ZCA23-00004) IN CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE.
  Staff report dated August 22, 2023, was presented to consider introduction of an ordinance
  approving Zoning Code Amendment No. 23-0004 (ZCA23-00004) in Chapter 12 of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code to establish regulations for fast food restaurants, Citywide.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing to be continued to the City Council Meeting of
  September 12, 2023, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 23-18 INTRODUCED -
  APPROVING ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 23-0005 (ZCA23-00005) TO
  MODIFY MISCELLANEOUS REGULATIONS IN CHAPTER 12 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (IMC). The City Clerk announced the next
  scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider introduction of an ordinance approving
  Zoning Code Amendment No. 23-00005 (ZCA23-00005) to modify miscellaneous
  regulations in Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) related to affordable
  housing, day-care regulations, and condominium regulations, Citywide, notice had been
  given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no
  communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the Staff Report dated August 22, 2023.

  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  2
 August 22, 2023

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke to address the Staff Report. He felt this was part of a
  bigger plan with Metro, the Inglewood Transit Connector, and favorable developers. He
  discussed transportation-oriented projects and the significance of decision-makers in the
  community. He also stated that he believed this was done to usher in market-rate
  condominiums and homes, expediting displacement. Additionally, the speaker added that
  when multi-million dollar buildings are built, it raises the property level or entices other
  corporate owners to operate the facilities under the guise of affordable housing. Finally,
